HFCL FY26 Annual Report Key Takeaways 🧵

• Strong FY26: Revenue grew 21.8% to ₹4,949 Cr, EBITDA +63.2% to ₹827 Cr and PAT +90.1% to ₹329 Cr.

• Margins expanding: EBITDA margin improved sharply to 16.7% from 12.5%, driven by better product mix and higher capacity utilisation.

• Business mix changing: Product-led revenue rose to 62% from 42%, while private customers increased to 84% from 65%.

• Exports taking off: Export contribution jumped to 41.4% from 12.2% in FY25, with >70% of cable production now serving international markets.

• Big global win: ₹10,159 Cr ($1.1B) OFC (Optical Fiber Cable) supply agreement with a global hyperscaler. Management targets exports at >50% of revenue by FY27.

• Strong visibility: Order book stood at ₹21,206 Cr in March 2026 and increased to ₹26,665 Cr by June 2026.

• Profitability is shifting: Telecom Products generated ₹2,931 Cr revenue and ₹764 Cr segment profit, while Turnkey Contracts generated ₹1,875 Cr revenue but a ₹113 Cr loss.

• Strategic pivot working: HFCL is moving from lower-margin project execution towards higher-margin, product-led businesses.

• Capacity expansion: OF capacity targeted at 38.5 mn fkm (fiber kilometer) and OFC capacity at 56.36 mn fkm by July 2028, with ~₹580 Cr being invested in backward integration into preforms.

• Defence opportunity: Defence revenue targeted at ₹500 Cr in FY27 vs ₹77 Cr in FY26, with a ~₹2,189 Cr defence/aerospace pipeline.

• Aerospace entry: Proposed acquisition brings an export-oriented ₹1,890 Cr order book, while a 1,000-acre defence facility is being developed in Andhra Pradesh.

• BharatNet optionality: HFCL has secured >₹7,335 Cr of Phase III contracts and sees upcoming opportunities worth >₹50,000 Cr.

• R&D focus: 229 R&D professionals are working across 5G, Wi-Fi, AI-enabled networking and emerging 6G technologies.

• Balance sheet: Debt increased to ₹1,713 Cr, but Net Debt/Equity remained comfortable at 0.34x.

• Key concern - cash flow: Operating cash flow was -₹335 Cr despite ₹329 Cr PAT, mainly due to higher inventory and receivables supporting the growing order book.

Overall, FY26 marks a meaningful transformation - from projects to products, domestic to global, and telecom towards a broader connectivity + defence + aerospace platform.

#QuestioningConvictionMuscle | Week ended 4 Sep 2026

The S&P 500 edged higher while Nifty fell for a fourth week.

Fear rose, yet volatility stayed subdued. Is this stress, rotation, or denial?

Market Pulse
S&P 500: +0.1%, closing 7,718.60.
Nifty 50: -1.2%, closing 23,897.70.

CNN Fear & Greed fell from 52, Neutral, to 42, Fear.
India's MMI fell from 49.46 to 43.87, both Fear.

US VIX ended at 14.53, up 0.10 point.
India VIX ended at 10.68, unchanged for the week despite a 5.8% Friday fall.

US and India Sector Divergence

US energy led as crude rose roughly 10%. Technology ranked next, but hardware strength hid a software selloff. Utilities also advanced. Equal-weight S&P 500 fell 0.8% while the NYSE 100 gained 0.7%, exposing narrow leadership beneath the flat headline index.

India was broader risk-off: 12 of 16 major sectors fell. Autos lost 4%, midcaps fell 1.5%, while smallcaps gained 0.1%. Coal India rose 3.6% on better earnings visibility. Capital-market stocks bounced Friday after SEBI said it would review derivatives settlement pricing. Price says selective rotation, sentiment says fear.

Announcements That Matter
• TCS, weekend: HyperVault secured 264 acres for a phased Hyderabad AI data-centre campus up to 1GW. TCS and partners expect investment up to ₹70,000 crore. The project is not operating. Watch customers, power and commissioning.

• Broadcom: Q3 revenue rose 86% to $29.6 billion. AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion, up 221%, while free cash flow was $13.7 billion. Q4 guidance is $34.8 billion. Watch whether growth holds without weaker margins.

• Nvidia: Agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion. Nvidia says the platform will remain open, multi-cloud and multi-accelerator. The strategic prize is developer distribution. Watch regulatory review and whether non-Nvidia hardware retains equal access.

• Sun Pharma: Joined nine manufacturers in US most-favoured-nation pricing agreements covering state Medicaid and future innovative medicines. The group committed at least $19.6 billion to US manufacturing. Watch company-specific pricing, capex and margin disclosure before assigning winners or losers.

• ICICI Bank and LIC, weekend: RBI approved LIC to lift its aggregate ICICI Bank holding to 9.99% of paid-up capital or voting rights within one year. Permission, not purchase. Watch shareholding disclosures.

• Adobe: Anil Chakravarthy will become CEO on 1 Dec; Shantanu Narayen moves to executive chair. With earnings due 10 Sep, the test is whether leadership change sharpens Adobe's AI monetisation story.

• Lululemon: Q2 revenue fell 4% and comparable sales fell 9%. Management guided Q3 revenue down 10% to 11% and FY2026 revenue down 5% to 7%. Watch Americas demand, markdowns and tariff-adjusted margins.

Small Company, Big Signal

E2E Networks signed a binding term sheet worth about ₹1,000 crore for Nvidia Blackwell cloud GPUs and services through June 2029, roughly four times FY2026 revenue. 

A term sheet is not recognised revenue. Billing milestones, customer concentration, utilisation and depreciation will decide the economics.

Cross-Border Government Signals

Global Signal, India Implication: BLS reported 162,000 US payroll additions in August. Resilient labour demand keeps US rate risk alive, raising the hurdle for Indian valuations and foreign flows.

India Signal, Global Implication: MoSPI reported Q1 goods-and-services exports up 25.8%, imports up 30.5% and machinery imports up 51.5%.

India is exporting faster while importing capital goods even faster, supporting global suppliers but increasing exposure to oil, currencies and financing costs.

Policy Winners & Losers

Potential winners include domestic data-centre suppliers and US manufacturing beneficiaries. 

Potential losers include pharma products exposed to lower public-program pricing. 

SEBI's settlement-price review may help market platforms, but final rules will determine the economics.

Consumer Temperature, Measured

RBI's July surveys covered 5,987 urban and 8,581 rural respondents. Current Situation indices fell to 88.3 from 90.7 in cities and 91.7 from 95.2 in rural areas. Yet non-essential-spending net responses improved to 3.3 from -0.8 urban and 32.4 from 30.1 rural. Households felt worse about conditions while reporting more discretionary spending.

Where Capital Is Crowding

US concentration is visible: equal-weight S&P 500 fell 0.8% while the NYSE 100 gained 0.7%, and hardware beat software. 

India's clearest crowding evidence remains primary markets: average IPO subscriptions rose to 59.1 times from 24.5 times, while listing gains climbed to 19.5% from 5.7%. 

AI announcements show capital clustering, but announcements alone do not prove a crowded trade. Watch breadth, pricing discipline and capex returns.

Greed & Pain

Greed sits in primary-market demand and the expanding AI-capex narrative, where announcements can be priced before utilisation and returns appear.

Pain sits in Indian autos, US consumer discretionary, software weakness and higher yields. The disagreement: fear gauges worsened, yet both volatility indices stayed low.

Failed Expectations

India's 7.8% real GDP growth did not lift Nifty. Strong US payrolls of 162,000 were good economic news, yet yields rose and the S&P 500 fell Friday. Good data did not mean easy money.

Week Ahead, 7 to 13 Sep

• 7 Sep: US markets closed for Labor Day.
• 10 Sep: US August PPI at 8:30 am ET. ECB decision at 14:15 CET, press conference at 14:45 and projections at 15:45. Oracle and Adobe report after the US close.
• 11 Sep: US August CPI at 8:30 am ET.

Inflation and the ECB will test the rate narrative. Oracle and Adobe will test whether AI spending is producing revenue beyond semiconductors.

Strongest Counterargument

The bearish read may be too neat. S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000 and Indian smallcaps gained while volatility stayed low. This may be rotation under pressure. Broader participation, easing yields and stable guidance would support that view. Rising volatility alongside weaker breadth and earnings cuts would refute it.

Conviction Check

• Is oil now the binding constraint for India's earnings and inflation?
• Can AI infrastructure earn returns before hardware depreciates?
• Does US software weakness challenge the AI monetisation story?
• Are IPO buyers pricing growth, scarcity, or exit liquidity?

One Rabbit Hole
Track who captures each ₹100 of AI spending: chips, networking, power, cooling, cloud operators, or software. That may matter more than capex headlines.

Which assumption in this week's market story would you challenge first?

We screened Q1 FY27 (April to June 2026) results for midcap CDMO names with 50%+ company-wide revenue growth.

Short answer: the list is thin. Most CRDMO players run mixed books (API plus formulations plus contract manufacturing), project timing is lumpy, and several of the cleanest names have already moved into largecap territory.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗰𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗻 𝗵𝗶𝘁

𝗡𝗲𝘂𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗟𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘀 (market cap around ₹25,000 crore)
Revenue up around 116 to 119% YoY to around ₹641 to 650 crore. Commercial CMS/CDMO projects did the heavy lifting, with export traction across Europe and the US. Margins expanded sharply alongside.

𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴, 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝟱𝟬%

𝗦𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗽𝗮 𝗠𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗲 (around ₹18,800 crore): revenue up 43 to 45%. Formulations more than doubled, specialty CDMO picking up.

𝗔𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗶 𝗣𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗯𝘀 (around ₹7,800 crore): revenue up 39 to 42%, with fresh capex announced for additional capacity.

𝗜𝗻𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗮 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝘁𝗮𝗯 (around ₹6,700 crore): revenue up 34%. CDMO segment, at around 70% of the book, grew around 32%.

𝗔𝗸𝘂𝗺𝘀 𝗗𝗿𝘂𝗴𝘀 (around ₹12,000 crore): topline up 14%, core CDMO revenue up 18 to 19%.

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗱 𝗕𝗶𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵 (around ₹16,400 crore): up 26%. API led, with CDMO ambitions.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝘇𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝘀 𝗱𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲

Laurus Labs reported CDMO revenue up around 67%, and Divi's CDMO grew around 50%. Both sit outside the midcap bucket, so they fall out of this screen even though the underlying trend is identical.

The structural story is intact: China plus one, more commercial stage work shifting to India, peptides, ADCs, complex chemistry.

But one quarter tells you very little in this business. Shipment timing and the development versus commercial mix can swing a quarter hard in either direction. What matters is order book conversion, client concentration and utilisation tracked across four to six quarters, not a single YoY print.

Gold financing stocks have had a strong year. IIFL up 50%, Manappuram 19%, FedFina 18%, Muthoot 3%, CSB down 8%.

Three things went right at once. Gold ran to records through FY26, which meant a lender could advance more against the same jewellery without changing anything about how it operated. Unsecured credit tightened after the microfinance mess, pushing borrowers toward the one asset most Indian households already own. And the RBI's new framework, which the market had braced for, landed friendlier than feared: more headroom on small consumption loans, no cap at all on income-generation loans, and no prior approval needed to open branches. That last one is why every lender in the group is suddenly expanding.

The first of those has now reversed. Domestic gold fell roughly 15% between the end of January and the end of June. That matters more in this sector than in most, because a gold loan book is short. It rolls inside a year, so it reflects current prices rather than prices from a long time ago. While the metal was rising, growth arrived without anyone having to do much. Now it has to come from grams pledged, and tonnage grows in single digits a quarter, not in the forties.

This is why FY27 guidance sits so far below what FY26 delivered. Muthoot grew 49% last year and is guiding 15% for this one.

The structural case is intact. Most gold lending in India still happens outside the formal system, with pawnbrokers and jewellers, and that share moves to organised lenders every year. Branch expansion is easier than it has been in over a decade. Demand from rural and semi-urban borrowers is steady and not especially rate-sensitive.

So the sector probably keeps growing. It just stops growing the easy way. FY26 was a year when the collateral did the work. FY27 is a year when the lender has to.

Coal India Output and Dispatch Set to Accelerate as Monsoon Effect Wanes

✅As the intense rains over coal command regions show clear signs of easing, coal production and supplies at Coal India Limited (CIL) are gathering pace and are set to improve further from here on. Despite prolonged spells of rain through July and August, particularly across the East-Central parts, CIL maintained a steady supply run. 

✅During April–August of the current fiscal, CIL supplied 322.90 million Tonnes (MT) of coal, 6.70% higher than the 302.60 MT supplied during the corresponding period last year.

✅The easing rainfall is already bringing relief on the ground. Coal beds that had turned sticky and wet after prolonged rain exposure are now drying out, making freshly mined coal free-flowing and considerably easier to transfer, handle and dispatch through Coal Handling Plants (CHPs). 

✅Coal seams at lower mine horizons that had been submerged are being restored to production through augmented pumping, while repair of internal haul roads is progressing in full swing.

✅Mines across CIL are consequently stepping up preparations to return to full operational pace, with the focus firmly on ensuring that production and coal movement pick up quickly as ground conditions continue to improve. 

✅While average daily coal production during the rain-affected first three days of September stood at around 1.36 MT per day, it rose to approximately 1.7 MT per day  on 04.09.2026, even with just a single day's respite from rain.
